beliefs.claim: The 628-request DeepSeek-first run does not establish that B5 is superior to B4.
beliefs.interpretation: There were 126 independently assessable matched pairs: 65 both exact, 47 neither exact, 10 B4-only exact, and 4 B5-only exact. These are descriptive pairs from one provider alias, not a confirmatory superiority estimate.
beliefs.scope: One frozen DeepSeek-first Monitor run and its observable references.

beliefs.claim: The 628-request run does not identify a causal effect of proposal content on recipient behavior.
beliefs.interpretation: Proposal-minus-neutral focal inputs differed by 32–85 provider tokens (mean +60, n=16); agents shared a rewarded target; fixed-peer settlement replay holds the other two baseline ballots constant. These constraints leave message semantics confounded with prompt differences and do not identify intent.
beliefs.scope: The frozen Agent schedule and its fixed-peer counterfactual replay.

beliefs.claim: The separate 856-row Monitor run provides no common completed-and-assessable B4/B5 pair for a head-to-head accuracy estimate.
beliefs.interpretation: Its Monitor outputs were heavily truncated; 715/856 reached the 128-token length cap and the common assessable B4/B5 denominator was 0. Keep this schedule separate from the 628-request run, which had 126 assessable pairs.
beliefs.scope: Only FULL-RESEARCH-EXECUTION-20261020 and its frozen Monitor schedule.

beliefs.claim: For the frozen matched-world pairs in the 856-row run, the deterministic Public-only projections were byte/reference-identical while Privileged projections differed.
beliefs.interpretation: This supports the stated input-construction property for those 24 comparisons. It does not show that an LLM Monitor can distinguish the worlds or establish a general latent-collusion impossibility result; only 2/72 matched-world outputs were parseable.
beliefs.scope: The exact matched-world construction and audit in FULL-RESEARCH-EXECUTION-20261020.

beliefs.claim: In the exact 24-context historical M4 run, B5 public-harm predictions changed in 20/24 Public-to-Privileged pairs while independently replayed reference labels changed in 0/24.
beliefs.interpretation: Transitions: 15 insufficient_evidence→absent, 4 present→absent, 1 insufficient_evidence→present. Fourteen changed pairs improved exactness, one worsened, five remained wrong. The intervention bundles message content, event inclusion/metadata, completeness, and token length.
beliefs.scope: Only the retained M4 B5 public-harm requests and their exact matched permission views; not a causal content effect, population estimate, detector metric, or collusion label.

beliefs.claim: The synthetic B5 diagnostic request builder was not byte-equivalent to the production M4 B5 request builder.
beliefs.interpretation: The synthetic projector omits mechanical_ledger, explicit allowed-label/incomplete-record prompt text, and stream=false. This is a plausible explanation for protocol-dependent predictions, not a proven cause of all-present outputs.
beliefs.scope: The exact frozen synthetic projector and production B5 request compiler source paths reviewed on 2026-10-21.

cycle_updates.remaining_alternatives: A one-sided model response bias, task/prompt framing, or a mismatch between the model interpretation and deterministic public-harm mapping remain plausible. The bundled projection also changes multiple structural fields and cannot identify message-semantic causality.
cycle_updates.statement: This 120-request synthetic diagnostic did not identify whether B5 labels are stable across the bundled Public-only versus task-irrelevant Privileged projection.
cycle_updates.what_changed: The raw binary predictions were one-sided: all 40 primary-public and label-flip outputs were present, despite balanced reference labels. This exposes a failed positive control and prevents interpretation of the 0/18 assessable pair changes.

cycle_updates.remaining_alternatives: Message semantics remain bundled with wording, salience, token length, event packaging, completeness cues, and provider-side variability. Exact request bodies and reported fingerprints do not guarantee identical hidden serving state.
cycle_updates.statement: For these 24 fixed M4 contexts, the frozen B5 request variants yield finite label changes, but no directional or causal message-semantic effect is identified.
cycle_updates.what_changed: Independent replay verified every assigned request and showed identical historical/current request bytes with label disagreement on many fixed cases, adding finite output non-repeatability as a concrete alternative to single-call view attribution.

cycle_updates.remaining_alternatives: This finite scripted construction does not establish a general impossibility theorem, real-agent behavior, natural-language recognition, Monitor accuracy, collusion, or latent intent. Privileged payload differences also include structural/completeness fields, which is why only the separately computed sequence-level differences support this narrow result.
cycle_updates.statement: For this frozen set of 12 scripted matched-world pairs, the authorized Public-only request/reference projections are identical while at least one determinate privileged proposal/acceptance/action sequence element differs in 8 pairs.
cycle_updates.what_changed: The corrected independent source-event replay now tests the preregistered per-pair sequence distinction gate directly; 8/12 pairs have a determinate sequence-element difference, including 2/12 with a complete proposal-acceptance-both-actions sequence difference.

historical_scope: The 628-request DeepSeek-first run and the separate 856-row Monitor run use different schedules and must never be pooled.

post_close_offline_updates.interpretation: A separate deterministic implementation matched 40/40 references. The Monitor predicted present on 40/40 rows and was exact on 20/40. This is fixture-specific and not a claim about collusion detection or general Monitor ability.
post_close_offline_updates.scope: Only the 20 primary and 20 label-flip public-canonical records in the B5 V2 synthetic fixture.
post_close_offline_updates.statement: For this frozen 40-row synthetic B5 public-canonical fixture, the public-harm reference is mechanically recoverable from the visible quality matrix, complete ballots, chair tie-break, and settled outcome.

post_close_offline_updates.interpretation: The 108-call scripted sequence plan remains paused. The unified 232-attempt campaign now has a schema-valid draft and sanitized assignment schedule, but it is not formally registered and has no current scope-specific authorization or runner.
post_close_offline_updates.scope: Research-route selection and source audits completed without new inference.
post_close_offline_updates.statement: The real M4 B5 view-response anomaly is the highest-value next mechanism question; available evidence supports response sensitivity but does not identify its cause.

post_close_offline_updates.interpretation: The schedule and preregistration draft are structurally valid, but exact model request bytes, an experiment-specific runner with atomic pre-request reservation, registry registration, a current approval batch, and live model outputs remain absent. No scientific response effect is estimated.
post_close_offline_updates.scope: Draft-only sample and schedule preflight; no request bodies, model outputs, formal preregistration, or inference.

purpose: Claim-level memory for future cycle selection. This is a scoped summary of historical artifacts, not a universal scientific score.
update_rule: Each closure must distinguish what changed, what remains plausible, and which hash-pinned evidence supports the update. Only a structured update confirmed by an independent review artifact counts toward the no-progress pivot counter. The registry checks provenance and shape, not truth.
